The decode loop is now its own module with its own tests, and the stream lifecycle is tested through the component. CameraScanner.tsx went 68% -> 100%, the frontend 94.8% -> 98.9% lines, with no coverage exclusion. Two things the work found: the post-loop 'if (!live) release()' was unreachable (nothing awaits between it and the check above), and a stream granted before a later failure was never released at all -- both fixed. inventory-tng-spk was raised for the decoder's poisoned promise, which is decoder.ts's own bug.

A Playwright test now drives a real getUserMedia stream carrying one of this project's own ECC-Q symbols and asserts the cart line: frontend/integration/decodes.spec.ts, with the clip built in frontend/integration/qrVideo.ts.

IT FOUND THE BUG IT WAS WRITTEN FOR, on its first run. The symbol carries the deep link (decision 0011 section 3), so the camera decodes HTTPS://INVENTORY.NYCMESH.NET/S/<code> -- and the app sent that whole string to GET /api/labels/{code}, which 404s. The in-app camera had never once worked against this project's own stickers, and neither suite could see it: every unit test feeds the scanner a bare code. Fixed by codeFromScan in frontend/src/scan/deepLink.ts, applied at the one funnel every scanned code passes through (useScannedCode), so a wedge scanner gun -- which reads the same symbol and types the same URL -- is fixed with it. Decision 0011 section 3 now records the obligation as well as the benefit, which is the gap that let this ship.

ON PODMAN AND ffmpeg, which the acceptance criteria asked to be settled: neither is needed, so neither question arises. Y4M is uncompressed frames behind a one-line header, so the clip is written directly in Node -- no container runtime, no rootless bind-mount uid problem, and nothing for a GitHub Actions runner to provide beyond the browser it already installs. The symbol is not invented either: the matrix comes from inventory.labels.symbol_for, so it is the project's own output at its own error correction level. One 640x480 frame, generated per run and deleted after, never committed.

WHAT IT DOES NOT CLAIM: the printed sticker's own readability, which the backend suite already asserts by decoding what segno drew with zxing-cpp. This test owns the handoff in between -- the ImageData frame.ts hands the decoder -- which was the risk in the description.

Verified non-vacuous: blank the film and the test fails.

The contract is in DEVELOPERS.md "Commits" -- one issue per commit, a 50-character imperative summary, a body saying what changed rather than how it was reached, one trailer naming the issue -- linked from CONTRIBUTING.md and AGENTS.md. Agents get the procedure at landing time from .agents/skills/commits/SKILL.md, which holds staging, the split-with-stash recipe for work that has already bled across two issues, and a worked good/bad message pair drawn from this repository's own history.

Kept by scripts/check-commit.sh rather than by memory: exactly one issue may move to closed in the .beads/issues.jsonl diff, while creating follow-up issues stays allowed. It also cross-checks the trailer against the tracker and reads the summary line. 17 tests in scripts/check-commit.test.sh, run in CI -- deliberately not run over a pull request's own messages, because the closure lives in a tracker contributors need not use and a squash merge composes its message after CI has run.

Two things the review caught that would have made it worse than useless. The documented wiring set core.hooksPath to a new directory, which would silently have disabled the beads hooks -- including the one that exports the very file the checker reads -- so it is now a symlink into .beads/hooks, which beads owns and leaves free. And the trailer rule demanded a bead id in a repository whose own docs say beads is not required, so "Closes #123" is now accepted and simply not cross-checked.

Proved on itself: this session's work was split with the procedure, and the gap that exposed -- a replaced commit already carries its own closure -- is now a --amend flag with tests of its own.
